learningObjective: Explain how one scalar-loss reverse sweep reuses cached forward values to produce a gradient for every parameter.
mediumRationale: A deterministic SVG is the smallest medium that can keep one computation graph fixed while separating the forward value-and-cache path from the reverse gradient path and its parameter-gradient branches.

mediumComparison.mermaid: Rejected: automatic routing cannot reliably align the same operations, cached values, and reverse branches in a compact interview-oriented trace.
mediumComparison.svg: Selected: fixed geometry can pair each operation with its cache, distinguish direction by arrowheads and line style, and remain a static accessible vector.
mediumComparison.semanticHtml: Rejected: a table can enumerate forward and backward work but cannot show that one reverse path branches into all parameter gradients as directly.
mediumComparison.interaction: Rejected: stepping through the passes adds controls and JavaScript without improving the single scalar-loss mental model.
mediumComparison.paperReuse: Rejected: no source figure with verified reuse permission isolates this article's cache-plus-one-reverse-sweep objective; the implementation is an original schematic.
mediumComparison.noVisual: Rejected: the prose gives the complexity result but leaves the reader to mentally connect the scalar seed, reverse traversal, cached activations, and simultaneous production of all parameter gradients.

pages.insight: The activation-functions slide discusses killed, unstable, and exploding gradients, providing the immediate conceptual lead-in but not the backpropagation algorithm.
The Learning section divider begins the contiguous deck section that contains backpropagation and optimization.
The gradient-descent-and-backprop title slide introduces the exact topic without adding a mechanism.

The Backprop Algorithm slide explains computational graphs, cached forward variables, chain-rule composition, branch-gradient addition, and matrix-gradient shapes; it is the directly relevant source-deck page.
The neighboring optimization slide contrasts random search, random local search, numerical gradients that scale linearly with parameter count, and gradient descent.
The next optimization slide moves to momentum, adaptive learning rates, and second-order methods, so it no longer adds detail about the reverse sweep.

deckReview.notes: The complete 214-page local deck was text-indexed for backprop, automatic differentiation, chain rule, gradient, cache, and numerical differentiation. Pages 41-46 were then read as the contiguous neighborhood around the only Backprop Algorithm slide. Page 44 supports the computation-graph and cache framing, while page 45 supports the O(P) numerical-differentiation contrast. The deck does not explicitly compare forward- and reverse-mode AD or provide a narrow reusable one-loss-to-all-parameters diagram. No deck image, wording, code, or layout is reused.

sources.title: Automatic Differentiation in Machine Learning: a Survey
sources.usage: Used to verify reverse accumulation, the one-output-many-inputs efficiency argument, and the distinction between automatic and numerical differentiation.
sources.license: No permissive figure-reuse permission was established for the article. No survey figure, wording, notation, or layout is copied; the shipped diagram is an original synthesis.

sources.title: PyTorch Autograd mechanics
sources.usage: Used as official framework documentation to verify that autograd records a directed acyclic graph, traces it backward with the chain rule, saves selected forward tensors for backward, and accumulates gradients into parameter leaves.
sources.license: PyTorch documentation is distributed with the BSD-3-Clause-licensed project. No documentation prose, code, or imagery is reproduced; only the documented semantics are cited.

sourceReview.notes: The hardest prose-only mental model is why reverse mode gets every parameter gradient from one scalar loss without perturbing each parameter separately: the forward pass creates one chain of values and saves operation-specific intermediates, then a single reverse sweep starts at dL/dL = 1, reuses those saved values in local vector-Jacobian products, and emits a gradient at every parameter leaf. The schematic is an original abstract three-operation network rather than an adaptation of either source.

agentReview.summary: Read the complete interview article, indexed the full 214-page deck and inspected the exact backpropagation neighborhood, then checked an authoritative AD survey and current PyTorch autograd documentation before selecting an original forward-cache/reverse-gradient trace.

implementation.accessibility: The SVG has a linked title and complete description. Forward flow is solid and points right; backward flow is dashed, points left, and terminates in three separately labelled parameter-gradient boxes, so meaning does not depend on color. Cache badges use both a distinct shape and explicit saved-value labels. The established backprop visual primitive provides a horizontally scrollable 42rem canvas at 390 CSS pixels, theme-token contrast in light and dark modes, and a print override that removes the minimum width and uses a high-contrast light palette.
